title: Transfusion medicine
subtitle: Consult and special processing · platelet refractoriness · transfusion reactions, TRALI vs TACO · blood bank workup, DAT, blood groups · apheresis, HDFN, storage, sickle cell · page 1 on-call consult, page 2 blood bank and board reference
source: Compiled from the Fellowship Transfusion Medicine review, The Fellow on Call ep. 060, and AABB / ASFA / ISBT guidance · primary sources verified against PubMed, October 2026.

blocks.heading: The consult
items: Transfuse for a physiologic reason, not a number. Trend, symptoms, bleeding and comorbidity outweigh the absolute value; a stable Hb of 6.8 from iron deficiency may need IV iron, not blood
What is the deficit? Hb, platelets, PT/INR + aPTT, fibrinogen, a specific factor
Bleeding or stable? Transfusion thresholds apply to non-bleeding patients; active hemorrhage is treated to clinical endpoints
Blood bank history: prior alloantibodies, prior reactions, anti-CD38 therapy, transplant (ABO switch), pregnancy
Special requirements: irradiated, antigen-negative, HLA-matched, washed (table below)
Goals / refusal: ask product by product (many who decline RBCs accept albumin, factor concentrates, cell salvage); plan IV iron, ESA, TXA, minimal phlebotomy
Single-unit policy: 1 RBC unit (or 1 apheresis platelet) → reassess before the next. Most over-transfusion is a reflexive 2-unit order
Stanford: Transfusion Medicine pager 12027 · Apheresis pager 19164 (650-725-4656) · Apheresis fellow 27283 · Special Coag lab 650-723-4813

blocks.heading: Special processing
rows: Inactivates donor T cells → prevents TA-GVHD. Allo-HSCT (from conditioning while immunosuppressed) · auto-HSCT (7 d before harvest → 3 mo post) · Hodgkin lymphoma, any stage — indefinitely · purine analogs: fludarabine, cladribine, pentostatin, bendamustine — indefinitely · alemtuzumab · congenital T-cell immunodeficiency · IUT/neonatal exchange · HLA-matched or relative-donated units, granulocytes · CAR-T per institutional policy. RBC shelf life drops to 28 d, K+ rises
Amotosalen/UVA — accepted alternative to irradiation; also mitigates bacterial risk
<5×10<sup>6</sup> WBC/unit. ↓ FNHTR, ↓ HLA alloimmunization/refractoriness (TRAP), ↓ CMV. Most US units are pre-storage LR
LR ≈ CMV-seronegative for HSCT, pregnancy, fetal/neonatal — either is acceptable
Removes plasma: recurrent severe allergic reactions, anaphylaxis with anti-IgA (or IgA-deficient donor), hyperkalemia risk
Known alloantibody; sickle cell: Rh (C, E) + K matched; anti-CD38 therapy (K-negative)

blocks.heading: Reactions
rows: Minutes. ABO mismatch (clerical) → intravascular hemolysis: fever, flank pain, hemoglobinuria, shock, DIC, AKI
Stop; fluids for urine output, pressors, treat DIC. Two-identifier bedside check
Antipyretic; diagnosis of exclusion. LR prevents
Pause, antihistamine, resume. No routine premed
Seconds–minutes; hypotension, bronchospasm. Anti-IgA in IgA deficiency (or haptoglobin deficiency)
Epinephrine. Check IgA; then washed or IgA-deficient products
High fever, rigors, shock; platelets (room temp) highest risk
Cultures (patient + bag), broad antibiotics; tell blood bank to quarantine co-components
3–14 d. Anamnestic alloantibody (Kidd classic) → Hb drop, ↑bili, DAT+ (IgG), new antibody
Usually supportive; antigen-negative units going forward
SCD: Hb falls below pre-transfusion; own + donor cells lysed, often DAT−
1–6 wk. Fever, rash, diarrhea, LFTs, marrow aplasia; >90% fatal
~5–10 d. Severe thrombocytopenia; anti-HPA-1a, classically multiparous women
Chronic transfusion (>~20 units) — heart, liver, endocrine

blocks.heading: Ordering and the bedside
items: Two-identifier bedside check of patient vs unit — the single most important ABO safeguard
Only normal saline in the line — LR's calcium clots citrated blood; hypotonic fluids hemolyze; no co-infused drugs
Finish each unit within 4 h of issue (bacterial growth). Typical RBC unit over 1–2 h; ~1 mL/kg/h if TACO-prone (HF, CKD, elderly, positive balance)
No routine premedication — acetaminophen/diphenhydramine did not reduce reactions in randomized trials; reserve for recurrent reactors
Consent covers reactions, TACO/TRALI and (very low) infection risk; document alternatives offered

chains.header: Any new sign during or after a transfusion
boxes: stop the unit; keep the line open with NS
vitals, airway, oxygen; epinephrine if anaphylaxis
re-check patient ID vs unit label at bedside
return bag + tubing; repeat type and screen
DAT, CBC, LDH, bili, haptoglobin, free Hb, UA
or hypotension; CXR + BNP if dyspneic
hives alone → allergic; may resume once resolved

blocks.heading: TRALI vs TACO
rows: Within 6 h; ARDS-like, no LAH. Type I (no ARDS risk factor) / II Vlaar 2019
Within 12 h; respiratory distress or pulmonary edema + ≥3 criteria ISBT 2018
Slow rate, single units, pre-emptive diuretic in at-risk
blocks.footnote: Report both to the blood bank. TRALI does not require antibody detection to diagnose.

blocks.heading: Platelet refractoriness
items: CCI = (post − pre count/µL) × BSA (m²) ÷ platelets given (×1011). 1-h CCI <5,000–7,500 on 2 consecutive ABO-compatible units = refractory
Good 1-h, poor 24-h → non-immune (most common): fever, sepsis, DIC, splenomegaly, bleeding, drugs (amphotericin), VOD/TA-TMA
Poor 1-h → immune: mostly HLA class I (HPA less often) → send HLA class I antibody screen → HLA-matched, antigen-avoidant, or crossmatch-compatible platelets, ABO-identical, irradiated
Also think drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia, HIT, PTP. Prevention = leukoreduction (TRAP: 13% → 3–5%)
Bleeding while refractory: keep transfusing + antifibrinolytic (TXA)

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — blood bank workup, DAT, apheresis, blood groups, ABO, HDFN, storage, sickle cell, key trials

blocks.heading: Blood bank workup
items: Type and screen = ABO/RhD + antibody screen (patient plasma vs reagent O cells, indirect antiglobulin test). Order it early in anyone likely to bleed
Crossmatch: electronic (screen negative + 2 concordant ABO types) → minutes. Full AHG crossmatch if an alloantibody is present
Positive screen → antibody ID panel → antigen-negative units — hours to days for multiple/rare antibodies. Call early in SCD, thalassemia, multiparous, chronically transfused
DAT (patient RBCs): IgG ± C3 → warm AIHA, DHTR, drug; C3 only → cold agglutinin, PCH
Warm AIHA: panreactive autoantibody; blood bank adsorbs to exclude hidden alloantibodies, then issues “least incompatible” units — never withhold blood in life-threatening anemia

Daratumumab / isatuximab (CD38 on reagent RBCs) → panreactive screen. Before first dose: type, screen + phenotype/genotype, tell the blood bank. Lab uses DTT-treated cells → DTT destroys Kell, so give K-negative units
Emergency release: uncrossmatched O-neg for females of childbearing potential and unknowns; O-pos for men and older women; AB plasma. Switch to type-specific ASAP
RhD-neg female of childbearing potential given RhD-pos platelets → RhIG (residual RBCs can immunize)
ABO-mismatched HSCT: blood bank picks the product group by transplant phase — don't override

blocks.heading: DAT patterns
rows: Warm AIHA (CLL, SLE, drugs), DHTR (mixed-field: only donor cells coated), HDFN, drug (penicillin, cephalosporins)
Cold agglutinin disease (IgM, Mycoplasma, LPL/Waldenström), PCH, immune-complex drug
Spherocytosis, G6PD, MAHA, PNH; DAT-negative AIHA (low-affinity IgG, IgA)
IVIG, ATG, recent RhIG; ~1 in several thousand healthy donors

blocks.heading: Apheresis — ASFA 2023 (pager 19164)
rows: Daily TPE — Cat I; start on suspicion (PLASMIC), don't wait for ADAMTS13. + steroids + caplacizumab (HERCULES: recurrence 12% vs 38%) ± rituximab
Leukocytapheresis — Cat III, not routine; prophylactic also III. Cytoreduce (hydroxyurea, induction). Avoid in APL
RBC exchange: acute stroke Cat I, stroke prophylaxis I, acute chest II. Target HbS <30%; avoid Hb >10–11
GBS, myasthenia gravis, CAPS, anti-GBM, ABO-incompatible / HLA desensitization (living-donor kidney)

blocks.heading: Blood groups and antibodies
rows: Naturally occurring IgM anti-A/anti-B (group O also IgG) → intravascular AHTR
O = universal RBC donor; AB = universal plasma donor; plasma compatibility runs in reverse
RhIG prevents anti-D only; passive anti-D makes the screen positive
IgG; DHTR, HDFN via erythroid suppression (anemia > bilirubin)
~91% of donors K-negative; McLeod (absent Kx) → acanthocytes
Fy(a−b−) common with African ancestry → P. vivax resistance + Duffy-null associated neutrophil count (benign low ANC)
Classic cause of DHTR — screen negative, then anamnestic boost
Anti-M/N usually cold IgM (insignificant); anti-S, s, U are significant
IgM, insignificant; antigens adsorbed from plasma
PCH — children after viral illness; DAT C3+
blocks.footnote: Clinically significant = IgG reacting at 37°C/AHG (Rh, Kell, Duffy, Kidd, S/s). Usually insignificant = IgM cold (Lewis, M, N, P1, I). Mnemonic: “Kidd kills, Duffy dies, Lewis lives.”

blocks.heading: ABO compatibility
blocks.footnote: RBCs: donor cells must lack the antigen the recipient's antibody sees. Plasma: the reverse. Platelets are given ABO-compatible when possible (out-of-group plasma can hemolyze; ABO-identical improves increments in refractoriness).

blocks.heading: HDFN and Rh immune globulin
items: RhD-neg mother: RhIG 300 µg at 28 wk + within 72 h of delivery of an RhD-pos baby, and after bleeding/procedures
One 300-µg vial covers 30 mL fetal whole blood (15 mL fetal RBCs)
Rosette screen → Kleihauer–Betke (or flow) to size the bleed: fetal blood (mL) ≈ KB% × 50; vials = mL ÷ 30, round up + 1
Once alloimmunized, RhIG is useless → titers, then MCA Doppler. Anti-K: titers unreliable — follow by Doppler
IV anti-D for ITP needs RhD-pos, spleen intact; risk of intravascular hemolysis

blocks.heading: Storage and infection risk
rows: Storage lesion: K<sup>+</sup> leak, ↓2,3-DPG — age did not matter clinically (ABLE, RECESS)
20–24°C with agitation; 5 d (7 d with FDA-approved bacterial testing)
Highest bacterial risk — FDA 2019 guidance: LVDS, secondary testing or pathogen reduction
Frozen ≤−18°C, 1 yr; thawed 24 h (thawed plasma 5 d at 1–6°C)
Frozen, 1 yr; use within 4–6 h of thaw/pool
blocks.footnote: Viral residual risk in high-income systems with NAT: HIV and HCV ~<1 per 1–2 million units; HBV somewhat higher. Non-infectious risks (TACO, TRALI, hemolysis) now dominate transfusion deaths.

blocks.heading: Sickle cell and chronic transfusion
items: Prophylactic Rh (C, E) + K antigen matching for all SCD transfusions; extended matching or RH genotyping if alloimmunized
Simple transfusion for symptomatic anemia; exchange to lower HbS (stroke, severe ACS, high-risk surgery). Never push Hb >10–11 — viscosity
DHTR in SCD mimics a pain crisis — check HbA% and a new antibody; hyperhemolysis = stop transfusing
Iron overload: chelate with deferasirox, deferoxamine or deferiprone (agranulocytosis — weekly ANC)

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Fresh (<8 d / ≤10 d) vs standard RBCs: no mortality or organ-dysfunction difference → don't request fresh units
AML: leukoreduced or UVB platelets cut alloimmune refractoriness 13% → 3–5%
iTTP caplacizumab + TPE: composite TTP death/recurrence/TE 12% vs 49%; recurrence 12% vs 38%
